seo.description: What ODD collects, why, who processes it, and how to change your cookie choices or exercise your rights under GDPR.

title: Privacy & cookies
intro: This page explains what happens to your information when you use allthingsodd.co or book ODDspace for an event — what we collect, why, who else processes it, and what you can ask us to do about it.

sections.title: Who is responsible
body: New Nordic Way rf, a registered non-profit association in Finland, is the data controller for this site and for ODDfest, ODDference, ODDspace and ODDagency. Our address is Sturenportti 3, Helsinki, Finland.
If you want to reach a person about anything on this page, write to hello@oddfest.co.

sections.title: What we collect, and when
body: We do not ask you to submit personal information just to read this site. When you choose to send information to us, this is what we collect:
items: Newsletter: your email address, and your name if you give it. Used to send you the ODD newsletter, and nothing else.

Business enquiries: your name, work email, organisation, what you are interested in, and what you want to achieve. We also record which page you came from and any campaign tags in the link you followed, so we can understand which ODD campaigns lead to enquiries.
Contact form: your name, email and message.

ODDfest event ideas: your name, email, phone number, organisation and website or portfolio, and what you tell us about the idea. We also record which page you came from and any campaign tags in the link you followed.

Tickets: your name, email, phone number and — if you are buying as a company — company name, VAT number and billing country. If you ask us to put a ticket in someone else's name, we store that person's name and email so we can admit them. We never see or store your card details; Stripe handles the payment itself.
Analytics: if, and only if, you accept the statistics category in the cookie banner, anonymised information about which pages you visit.

Venue bookings: the name, contact details and organisation of the organiser and its contact persons, billing details, and the names of the security steward and crew who need access to the building. Some of this is given to us by the organiser rather than by you.

sections.title: The legal basis for each of those
body: Newsletter and analytics run on your consent, which you can withdraw at any time — the unsubscribe link in any newsletter, and the cookie settings on this page.

Ticket purchases run on performance of a contract: we cannot sell you a ticket and let you in without knowing who you are. Some of that data we keep afterwards because Finnish accounting law requires us to.
Enquiries and messages you send us run on our legitimate interest in answering people who contact us.

Venue bookings run on performance of the booking contract and, for contact persons and crew named by the organiser, on our legitimate interest in running events safely. We keep invoices because Finnish accounting law requires us to.

sections.title: Who else processes it
body: We use a small number of external services for specific jobs. Their roles and purposes are listed below:
items: Google Analytics (Google Ireland Limited) — anonymised usage statistics. Only after you accept.

items.text: Behold (Behold Studio, Inc.) — serves the Instagram gallery on the ODDspace pages. It sets no cookies and stores nothing on your device; your browser requests the photographs from Behold’s servers the same way it requests any other image.

items: Stripe Payments Europe, Ltd. — ticket payments and payment fraud prevention.
beehiiv, Inc. — sending the newsletter.
Attio — our internal record of business enquiries, so an enquiry does not get lost.
Notion Labs, Inc. — our internal record of ODDspace venue booking enquiries and bookings, and of ODDfest event ideas.
Resend — delivering contact-form messages to our inbox, and emailing us a booking enquiry or event idea that could not be filed straight away.
Cloudflare, Inc. — hosts the website and runs the services behind our forms and ticketing.

sections.title: Where your data goes
body: Some of these providers are based in, or store data in, the United States. Where that is the case, transfers rely on the EU–US Data Privacy Framework or on the European Commission's standard contractual clauses.
We do not sell your personal data, and we do not share it with anyone for advertising.

For venue bookings, we share the names and contact details of the organiser's contact person, security steward and relevant crew with the building's owner and its property maintenance and security providers, where needed for building access and alarm arrangements. They use the data as separate controllers.

sections.title: How long we keep it
body: Newsletter subscriptions: until you unsubscribe.
Enquiries and messages: while the matter is active and for up to two years after the last interaction.
Ticket and payment records: six years, which is what Finnish accounting law requires.
Analytics: for the retention period set on our Google Analytics property, currently 14 months.
Venue bookings: booking records for three years after the event; invoices for six years, as Finnish accounting law requires.

sections.title: Your rights
body: Under the GDPR you can ask us to do any of the following, free of charge, and we will answer within one month:
items: Access — get a copy of what we hold about you.
Rectification — have anything inaccurate corrected.
Erasure — have your data deleted, unless we are legally required to keep it.
Restriction — have us pause processing while something is disputed.
Portability — receive your data in a machine-readable format.
Objection — object to processing we base on legitimate interest.
Withdraw consent — at any time, without affecting anything done before you withdrew it.

sections.title: If you are not satisfied
body: Write to us first — most things are quicker to fix directly. If we cannot resolve it, you have the right to complain to the Finnish Data Protection Ombudsman (Tietosuojavaltuutetun toimisto), tietosuoja.fi.

sections.title: Changes to this page
body: If what we do changes, this page changes with it, and the date at the top changes too. A material change to what we collect or who processes it will also reset the cookie banner so we can ask for consent again.
